$comment: S0 is evaluated FIRST and cannot be disabled. A network mismatch means every subsequent comparison would be made against the wrong world, so nothing after it is meaningful. Three things must agree: the key's prefix, the agent's network, and the network named in the challenge.

cases.name: pass · a sandbox key, a sandbox agent and a sandbox challenge
fail · a test key presented for a mainnet agent
fail · a live key presented for a sandbox agent — a test key must never spend real money
boundary · the key and the agent agree, but the CHALLENGE names the other network
cases.$why: This is the half-implemented version of the rule: a check that only compares the key prefix to the agent waves this through, and the agent then pays against the wrong network's mint.

cases.name: fail · S0 wins even when the agent is also killed
cases.$why: Evaluation order is part of the contract. The SDK branches on the code, so a killed agent with a network mismatch must always report the same one.
